answer: The basalt graph is validated at intake and the harbor frontier is published, and as a result the ancestry of every answer is public, and ripple anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 363 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. A farm of 294 pays that 88 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
